description: Recent studies showed that single nucleotide polymorphisms (rs3217992,a>g,rs1063192,c>t) mapping in the vicinity of anril are linked to a wide spectrum of conditions,including cardiovascular disease,ischemic stroke,type 2 diabetes,frailty and alzheimer's disease.

Risk snps (rs3217992,a>g,rs1063192,c>t) for coronary disease,stroke,diabetes,melanoma,and glioma were all associated with allelic expression of anril.

While the exact role of anril awaited further elucidation,common disease genomewide association studies (gwas) have surprisingly identified the anril gene as a genetic susceptibility locus shared associated by coronary disease,intracranial aneurysm and also type 2 diabetes.

Quantitative reverse transcriptase pcr analysis showed that silencing anril resulted in an increase of p15ink4b expression by nearly 8-fold,but had minimal effect on the expression of p16ink4a (increased by 1.8-fold) or p14arf.Rna immunoprecipitation demonstrates that anril binds to suz12 in vivo.Therefore,it is possible that the deregulation of anril by such risk-associated single-nucleotide polymorphisms changes the expression level of p15ink4b and/or other target genes,leading to the development of type 2 diabetes or coronary heart disease in humans.
Furthermore,genome wide association studies have identified the anril gene as a risk locus for coronary disease,intracranial aneurism,type 2 diabetes and several cancers including glioma.

Risk snps for coronary disease,stroke,diabetes,melanoma,and glioma were all associated with allelic expression of anril (all p<0.05 after correction for multiple testing),while association with the other two genes was only detectable for some risk snps.Snps had an inverse effect on anril and cdkn2b expression,supporting a role of antisense transcription in cdkn2b regulation.Our study suggests that modulation of anril expression mediates susceptibility to several important human diseases.

Anril is a recently discovered long non-coding rna encoded in the chromosome 9p21 region.This locus is a hotspot for disease-associated polymorphisms,and it has been consistently associated with cardiovascular disease,and more recently with several cancers,diabetes,glaucoma,endometriosis among other conditions.
